page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. The instance is configured with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of the n1-highmem-4 in the lower tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, fall into the bottom 25% category. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests show weak results, with read-only large block bandwidth at 25.86 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 21.97 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench image processing scores are in the bottom 10% tier, reflecting the older architecture of the Intel Xeon CPU.

This instance offers a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio than standard general-purpose instances, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed compute. However, the tradeoff is significantly lower processing throughput, as demonstrated by the weak Passmark CPU score of 3477.62 and poor LLM inference speeds. The n1-highmem-4 is suitable for moderate database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive applications that are not CPU-bound.
